summary: A state-funded commuter bus to a large work site cut about an hour each way for people on a long trip from home to a shift.
realLife: A new Baltimore County route runs from the east side to a big industrial site with about 15,000 workers and more expected. It cuts commutes by about an hour each way, and some who faced about an hour and a half now have a direct ride. Fares were $4 one way and $136 for a monthly pass. Buses run from early morning to just before 1 a.m., which fits many shift starts and ends. A $2 million state investment paid for it.
